_comment: WHAT EACH SCREEN'S CONTROLS CAN DO TO THE APPLICATION — the input the compiler uses to establish a step's risk class, and the one thing neither a trace nor a model can supply. Keyed on canonical SYMBOLS so it serves every tenant running MERIDIAN MSC 4.2, exactly as the artifact and the policy's screenRules are. A screen that is absent here does not get a safe default: the compiler REFUSES, and a discovery run refuses to act. That is deliberate — the label this file replaced was `read_only` stamped on every step, which read as a measurement and was an assumption.

screens.note: Authenticates a session; it changes no member record. The passcode field is a credential rather than a risk class — safety/redact.ts masks it by field name, and a policy's deniedFields is where automation is stopped from filling one.
Navigation only. Every control is a link to another screen.
A query form. Filling it and submitting it runs a lookup; mock/main.ts answers /screen/results with a pure read and appends no audit row.
A results grid whose only controls open a member. Reading, not writing.
A read-only servicing view. Its one link leads to card services, which is where anything can change.

THE ONLY SCREEN FROM WHICH THIS APPLICATION CHANGES ANYTHING (mock/main.ts: POST /screen/card-action is its single mutating route). Rated at the screen rather than at the submit, because a form's fields and its submit are one transaction: the value typed into ACTION is what decides what commits. FREEZE and UNFREEZE are the two codes reachable without supervisor authority, and both are reversible by re-running the same capability with the opposite code.

controls.note: Supplying the supervisor override is what unlocks LOST_STOLEN, the one status this application cannot undo (mock/actions.ts refuses it with MSG 0140 when the field is empty). A plan that types one is therefore rated irreversible whatever else it does, which under the shipped policy (irreversible: confirm) means it escalates to a person instead of running unattended.

screens.note: The transaction has already committed by the time this renders. Nothing on it acts; a capability reads its confirmation number and stops.
